solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: It's material how Spooner's cat attacked soup

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the two words here trade their starts

parts.note: a cat that attacked clawed
broth is a thin soup

explanation.surface: A garbled tale of a cat savaging some soup, offered as a description of a fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening sounds of CLAWED BROTH gives a phrase sounding like BROAD CLOTH.
explanation.definitionFit: Broadcloth is a fine, densely woven fabric, originally of wool, so it is a kind of material.

clue.text: Your uncle perhaps rises and falls

definitions.meaning: from the British catchphrase meaning 'there you are', a man called Bob is your uncle
to bob is to move up and down on water

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bob's your uncle' is a British saying meaning 'and there you have it'; the clue reads it literally.
explanation.definitionFit: The catchphrase contraction and the verb for bouncing up and down on a surface share one spelling.

clue.text: Bond villains which are executed around the house

definitions.meaning: Oddjob is the hat-throwing henchman in Goldfinger; the plural is jokey

definitions.text: which are executed around the house
definitions.meaning: small domestic tasks and repairs carried out at home

explanation.walkthrough: 'Executed' suggests killing to fit the villains, but here it just means carried out.
explanation.definitionFit: Small miscellaneous chores done in a home are known by this name, and the henchman shares it.

clue.text: Film star was super-attractive to Manilow

parts.note: with 'attractive to', was attractive to means drew (pulled in)
Barry Manilow is the American singer
the 'super' makes the attraction greater: more

explanation.surface: A singer is said to find someone irresistible.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'was super-attractive to Manilow' as the phrase 'drew Barry more', i.e. attracted Barry more strongly.
explanation.definitionFit: Drew Barrymore is an American actor known for films such as E.T. and Charlie's Angels.

clue.text: In Honolulu there is a turbulent priest

indicators.note: signals that the answer lies inside the run of letters of the words Honolulu there

explanation.surface: A troublesome clergyman is found in Hawaii.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turbulent priest' echoes Henry II's line about Becket, but here it is the reformer.
explanation.definitionFit: Martin Luther was the German monk and priest whose defiance of Rome sparked the Reformation.

clue.text: Pancake beginning to titillate men Swinton left for dead

indicators.note: the beginning of the word titillate means its first letter

parts.note: OR is the abbreviation for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

indicators.note: L (left) replaces D (dead) in the name

parts.note: Tilda Swinton is the British actor

explanation.surface: A pancake starts to excite the men while an actor is abandoned.
explanation.walkthrough: TILDA with L for D gives TILLA.
explanation.definitionFit: A tortilla is a thin flat Mexican bread made of maize or wheat, resembling a pancake.

clue.text: Cultivate key member

parts.note: F is a musical key
an arm is a limb, a member of the body

explanation.surface: An instruction to develop an important member of a group.
explanation.definitionFit: To farm land is to grow crops on it, i.e. till and cultivate it.

clue.text: Plants one last beer on a coaster's centre

parts.note: A as the indefinite article means one
Z is the last letter of the alphabet
ale is a kind of beer

indicators.note: the centre of the word coaster is its middle letter

explanation.surface: Plants, then one final beer set down on a coaster.
explanation.definitionFit: Azaleas are flowering shrubs of the rhododendron family, hence garden plants.

clue.text: Fancy dress party compelled to hold square dance

indicators.note: one word holding another means it surrounds it

parts.note: made someone do something means compelled them

indicators.note: letters made to dance are jumbled about

explanation.surface: Guests at a costume ball are forced into a square dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dance' looks like part of the party scene but is the anagram signal; 'Fancy' belongs to the definition, not an anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A masquerade is a ball where guests wear masks and costumes.

clue.text: English medic in top sort of treatment

indicators.note: the English medic pieces sit inside the word for top

parts.note: best means top, finest
DR is the abbreviation for doctor

explanation.surface: An English doctor at the top of the field prescribes a particular cure.
explanation.definitionFit: Being told to stay lying down to recover is a prescribed form of medical treatment.

clue.text: Warms up food behind woman's back

indicators.note: the food word is placed behind, after the reversed piece
the woman's word is read backwards

parts.note: her, the woman's possessive pronoun
eats is slang for food

explanation.surface: Someone warms up dinner behind a woman's back.
explanation.definitionFit: To heat food again is to warm it up, the same verb form.

clue.text: 3d film

definitions.meaning: three old pence, half the value of a sixpence coin; it looks like 3-D
the 1967 musical film starring Tommy Steele

explanation.walkthrough: '3d' looks like three-dimensional cinema but is three old pennies; d was the pre-decimal British penny and a sixpence was a coin worth six of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Three pre-decimal pennies are exactly half the old sixpence coin, and the musical film bears that title.

clue.text: Gates and Clinton performing separately in the same show?

definitions.text: Gates and Clinton performing separately in the same show?

parts.words: Gates and Clinton performing separately in the same show?
parts.note: Bill Gates and Bill Clinton are two Bills, and two separate acts on one programme form a pair of features

explanation.surface: Two famous Bills appear on stage in one evening.
explanation.definitionFit: A programme of two films or plays shown one after the other is a two-feature evening, here punning on two Bills.

clue.text: Match Australian native, not before time

parts.note: the emu is a large flightless bird native to Australia
arriving after the due time is late

explanation.surface: A sports fixture involving an Australian is overdue.
explanation.definitionFit: To emulate someone is to equal or rival them, i.e. to match them.

clue.text: Loot San Francisco, say, to be a killjoy

parts.note: spoils are plunder, loot
San Francisco is an example of a port, a harbour city

explanation.surface: Plundering a Californian city is the act of a spoilsport.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoilsport ruins other people's fun, exactly what a killjoy does.

clue.text: Old railway croissant?

parts.note: past means former, old

explanation.surface: A stale croissant from an old railway buffet.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A croissant is an example of a baked item made from flaky dough.

clue.text: Is inclined to enter church — in the end, prayer is what purifies

indicators.note: one piece entering another goes inside it

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
leans means is inclined, tilts

indicators.note: the end of the word prayer is its last letter

explanation.surface: A churchgoer bows into prayer, which cleanses the soul.
explanation.definitionFit: A cleanser is a substance that cleans, removing impurities.

clue.text: Omitting the first two, washes each submarine

indicators.note: the opening two letters of the washing word are dropped

parts.note: launders means washes

explanation.surface: Washing each submarine while skipping the first couple.
explanation.walkthrough: LAUNDERS loses LA to give UNDERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Submarine as an adjective means located beneath the waves, as does this word.

clue.text: Meaning the rest of the House of Commons are telling the truth?

definitions.text: the rest of the House of Commons are telling the truth?
definitions.meaning: if I alone of the members am the liar, everyone else must be honest

explanation.walkthrough: The second half reads the answer as 'I MP lying', a confession that implies all other MPs are truthful.
explanation.definitionFit: To suggest something without stating it outright is to mean it indirectly.

clue.text: Things Shakespeare wrote and wrote with juvenile restraint

parts.note: Shakespeare wrote dramas, each one a play
a pen is what one writes with

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's works and his quill, followed by a toddler's enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: A playpen is a portable enclosure that keeps a baby or toddler safely confined.

clue.text: Be bothered by holding curate's clothing cut into small pieces

indicators.note: one word holding another wraps around it

parts.note: to mind is to be bothered by something

indicators.note: the clothing of the word curate is its outer pair of letters

explanation.surface: Being upset by a clergyman's garments being shredded.
explanation.walkthrough: The outer letters of curate are C and E.
explanation.definitionFit: Minced meat or onion has been chopped very finely, i.e. cut into tiny bits.

clue.text: Play this card first, then the last spade, in case the ace is needed

indicators.note: the first of the word card is its opening letter
the last of the word spade is its final letter

parts.note: lest means in case, for fear that
A is the abbreviation for ace on playing cards

explanation.surface: Bridge advice on the order to play cards in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play' looks like the card-game verb, but 'Play this' asks for an instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A celesta is a keyboard instrument with metal bars, so it is something one plays.

clue.text: Regularly bars old worker sloping away?

indicators.note: taking every second letter of the words bars old at regular intervals

parts.note: a worker ant is the usual crossword worker

explanation.surface: An old labourer often barred from work slinks away.
explanation.definitionFit: Aslant means at a slant, sloping or oblique.

clue.text: Music from Saskatchewan

indicators.note: the answer is taken from within the letters of the province name

explanation.surface: Some music from a Canadian province.
explanation.definitionFit: Ska is a Jamaican genre of popular music, a forerunner of reggae.

clue.text: Provide too much too flexibly

parts.note: over means too, excessively, as in over-eager
supply as an adverb means in a supple, flexible way

explanation.surface: Giving too much, too pliably.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flexibly' is SUPPLY as an adverb from supple, not the verb supply.
explanation.definitionFit: To give more than is needed is to provide an excess, a glut.

clue.text: See 13
Shore up trembling musician

indicators.note: letters that tremble are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: A nervous musician being propped up.
explanation.definitionFit: Orpheus is the legendary Greek musician whose lyre playing charmed beasts and the underworld.

clue.text: Forgetting names worried current archivist at the outset

indicators.note: worried letters are fretted out of shape and rearranged

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current

indicators.note: the outset of the word archivist is its first letter

explanation.surface: A record keeper anxiously forgets names.
explanation.definitionFit: Amnesia is loss of memory, the condition of forgetting.

clue.text: Gets Brown, primarily to annoy Nicola Sturgeon

indicators.note: primarily picks out the first letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: Gordon Brown irritates Nicola Sturgeon, the former Scottish First Minister.
explanation.walkthrough: Brown looks like the former UK Prime Minister, rival of Scotland's Sturgeon, but it is the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who tans becomes darker in the sun, i.e. gets brown.

clue.text: Feed pet Ancient Briton brought back, having taken heart

parts.note: a cat is a typical pet

indicators.note: the Briton word is brought back, read in reverse

parts.note: the Celts were the ancient inhabitants of Britain

indicators.note: the heart of the word taken is its middle letters

explanation.surface: A pet is fed by an Ancient Briton who returned with courage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought back' turns CELT into TLEC; 'taken heart' gives AKE.
explanation.definitionFit: Cattle cake is compressed concentrated fodder given to livestock, a type of animal feed.
